summary: Kootenai County, Idaho: 1931 pole tower, 1946 L-4 tower moved from Echo Peak, cab sold in 1963; a 2025 visit found the tower still there without its cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com names the Idaho Dept. of Lands and Peakbagging.com places the site on Idaho state land; Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Coeur d'Alene National Forest instead. The state-land listing fits the Idaho Dept. of Lands entry, which is kept.

The Forest Fire Lookout Association list says ruins. Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say the superstructure remains, and a 2025 WillhiteWeb visit found the tower still there without its cab. The record's ruins status is kept, with the caveat in status_note.
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 6,400 feet. WillhiteWeb gives 6,408 feet for the summit and 6,360 feet for the Twin Crags point. The record's 1950.7 m (6,400 ft) is kept.
The 1946 origin of the moved tower is Echo Peak on Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com and Echo Lookout on WillhiteWeb. The story uses Echo Peak and notes WillhiteWeb's wording.

sources.title: Latour Peak and Twin Crags Lookout

notes_for_editor: The record's status 'ruins' is kept. The brief's conflict note says firelookout.com reads 'standing', but that page says 'Superstructure remains still there.' No source gives an access level, so none is set; the story says so. The 1946 windstorm year comes from peakbagging.com only, and Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give no year for the storm. Staffing names are from two lookout-history sites, not checked against the cited photo collection or newspaper. Used 1 search and 5 page reads.
